clue.text: Old prison dispute spoken of, in court

parts.note: quad, or quod, is old slang for a prison

indicators.note: spoken of says the next word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to dispute noisily is to wrangle

explanation.surface: An old gaol row is discussed in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' here is the open courtyard of a college, not a court of law; WRANGLE said aloud gives RANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard enclosed by buildings, as at an Oxford college, is a quad of this kind.

clue.text: Man's house said to provide moorings

indicators.note: said signals that the word is only pronounced like the letters entered

parts.note: the House of Keys is the lower house of the Isle of Man's parliament

explanation.surface: A man's home is reported to supply places to tie up boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, whose parliament has a chamber called the House of Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Wharves where vessels tie up are places of mooring for boats.

clue.text: European mounts first of ads, : supported by British chain

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top, held up by what follows
first of picks just the opening letter of the word ads

parts.note: the Pennines are a range of hills in northern England

explanation.surface: A mountain range in Europe is propped up by a British chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The range running down the length of Italy is a set of European mountains.

clue.text: Bob, perhaps, used to add variety thus

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer's call used to vary things.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob is a call in change ringing that alters the order the bells sound in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to peal bells in varying orders and, figuratively, to vary one's routine.

clue.text: Discover capital finally goes in no time

indicators.note: in places the shortened city between the two pieces of no time

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally goes means the closing letter of the city is dropped

parts.note: Seoul is the capital of South Korea

explanation.surface: Find out that a city's end goes in no time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To sniff something out is to find it by searching, like a dog following a scent.

clue.text: Everybody upset over emperor resident in South America

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second
in a down clue upset turns the word for everybody upside down

parts.note: everybody means all
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: Everyone is overturned over an emperor living in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A plainsman or cowboy of the Venezuelan grasslands is a South American dweller.

clue.text: Man's device for parts of fixture

explanation.surface: An emblem of a man and pieces of a sporting match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man's emblem is three running limbs; a two-match tie is played in two halves of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx flag shows three bent limbs, and each match of a home-and-away tie is one stage of it.

clue.text: Be a prejudiced person, not using head

indicators.note: not using head says the first letter of the bigot's word is dropped

parts.note: a sexist is someone prejudiced against one sex

explanation.surface: A bigot is told to be one without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is to have being, to live or be present.

clue.text: Island filled with music — temperature appears to rise sharply

indicators.note: filled with puts the music inside the island

parts.note: Skye is a Scottish island
rock is a kind of popular music

explanation.surface: A Scottish island full of music sees its temperature shoot up.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that soar shoot up fast, like a firework launched into the air.

clue.text: To a chatterer, I'd furiously delivered a stern warning

indicators.note: furiously suggests a wild jumbling of these letters

explanation.surface: Someone angrily rebukes a gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' rearranges the letters of TO A CHATTERER and ID; the Riot Act was read to disperse crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish someone sternly is idiomatically to read them the act once read to disperse rioters.

clue.text: A goddess crossing river in: entrance to underworld

indicators.note: crossing means the goddess straddles the river, holding it within her

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love

explanation.surface: A goddess fords a river in the gateway to Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman poets placed the way into Hades at Lake Avernus near Naples.

clue.text: Useful feature you can make any time

indicators.note: you can make signals building a new word out of the letters given

explanation.surface: A handy facility available whenever you like.
explanation.definitionFit: A facility that adds comfort or convenience, such as a pool or shop, is an amenity.

clue.text: Decomposed rose stunk as a : result of overheating

indicators.note: decomposed means broken down, so these letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A rotting flower smelt awful because it got too hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Collapse from too much sun on the head is an illness caused by overheating.

clue.text: Backed to excess, I 'would repeat

indicators.note: backed means both pieces together are written in reverse order

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means to excess
I'd is short for I would

explanation.surface: Turned too far, I would do it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' reverses OTT plus ID, giving DI then TTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the same again, used to show something is repeated.

clue.text: Char wrong, say, to retire

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: to retire means to go back, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: say means for example, EG

explanation.surface: A cleaner is mistaken, as it were, to quit work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like a cleaning lady (British) but is the verb to scorch; 'to retire' reverses EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch lightly on the surface is to burn slightly.

clue.text: Beggar allowed to wear jumpers upside down?

indicators.note: to wear means the lawful word is clothed by the jumpers around it
upside down in a down clue reverses the animals' word

parts.note: roos, kangaroos, are jumpers
licit means allowed or lawful

explanation.surface: A lawful item worn with inverted sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' are not sweaters but kangaroos; 'upside down' turns them over, giving SOOR, which wraps the lawful word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: one who solicits, asking for money or favours, can be called a beggar.

clue.text: It would be extremely slow tackling onset of plaque

definitions.text: It would be extremely slow tackling onset of plaque

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, so the phrase wraps round the letter

parts.note: too thick means exceedingly slow-witted

indicators.note: onset of picks the opening letter of plaque

explanation.surface: Someone sluggish going after the start of dental plaque.
explanation.walkthrough: TOO THICK goes round P; the whole clue also describes the little stick that tackles plaque.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed stick for cleaning between teeth deals with plaque.

clue.text: Reconditioned big limo, 'or old heap

indicators.note: reconditioned means rebuilt, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A big limousine done up, or an old banger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reconditioned' rearranges BIG LIMO and OR; 'old heap' suggests a car but is an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word first meant a confused pile, before its sense of a tangled situation.

clue.text: Hotels are unlikely to become discouraged

indicators.note: unlikely here means improbable, so these letters form an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: Hotels are not likely to get disheartened.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose courage or hope is to become dispirited.

clue.text: In books, one can check two examples of gold coin, once it's included

indicators.note: it's included says the old coin is placed within the gold pair

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
or is gold in heraldry
a dit, or doit, was an old Dutch coin of little value

explanation.surface: Inside a ledger, someone can verify two gold pieces and an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant who inspects a firm's accounts is checking its books.

clue.text: Opera the French cut down proportionately

parts.note: Tosca is an opera by Puccini
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An opera reduced by the French in proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn or reduced in exact proportion to the original is so made.

clue.text: Capital place for a battle? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely says the city lies within these words, using only part of them

explanation.surface: A city where a battle might be fought, though not wholly.
explanation.walkthrough: The city sits inside 'foR A BATtle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Morocco is a capital city.

clue.text: Murderer hanging about ..- bishop's dwelling

indicators.note: hanging about means surrounding, so the murderer wraps the bishop

parts.note: Cain killed Abel in Genesis
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A killer lurks round a bishop's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hut or simple house is a humble dwelling.

clue.text: One hiding in outhouse as a child

indicators.note: hiding in puts one inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a barn is a farm outbuilding
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone hides in a shed as a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRN is Scottish and northern English for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word for a young child is used across northern Britain.

clue.text: Dirty dance with dirty look

parts.note: a disco is a dance
to lour is to scowl or give a sullen look

explanation.surface: A grimy dance with a filthy glare.
explanation.definitionFit: To stain or mark something spoils its colour, making it dirty.

clue.text: Colour I had repeated

parts.note: red is a colour
I'd is short for I had

explanation.surface: Colour that I had done again.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something over again is to have done it a second time.

clue.text: Free temporary cover put round missile

indicators.note: put round means the cover encloses the other word

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A loose tarpaulin wrapped around a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trident is a submarine-launched nuclear missile, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Girl I guided and served

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
led means guided

explanation.surface: A girl I steered and helped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that availed you was of use, helping or serving you.

clue.text: Complete row of squares

explanation.surface: A total line on a chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: On a chessboard the horizontal rows are called ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means utter, as in a total beginner, and a horizontal line of chessboard squares.

clue.text: Impertinently questions origin of the poet's vocation

parts.note: to pry is to ask nosy questions

indicators.note: origin of picks the first letter of the word the

parts.note: Thomas Hood was an English poet

explanation.surface: Nosy questioning starts a poet on his calling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordination as a clergyman is a religious calling.
